data.description:
## Summary

The shared test runner (skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py) defines a static NODE_SUITE_DIRS = (tests/node, tests/cli, tests/unit). ContextHub has no tests/node directory (git ls-files confirms it was never tracked), so the canonical full-suite command npm --silent test -- tests/node always exits 1 with 'No test files found'.

## Impact

The audit skill's automatic full-suite verification (SA-0MSIU5HFI0024D7W) queries the per-repo test cache for EVERY canonical suite command and requires exit code 0. The permanently-failing tests/node entry means the audit runner can NEVER inject automatic green-run evidence for ContextHub audits — execution-dependent acceptance criteria (e.g. 'Full project test suite passes') stay partial and block closure.

## Workaround used in release v1.0.9

Operator ran pytest (103 passed) + npx vitest run (4117 passed) at the release HEAD and passed --green-run HEAD to each audit — honest attestation, but manual.

## Suggested fix

Either (a) filter NODE_SUITE_DIRS by directory existence in the shared runner, or (b) make ContextHub's suite definition explicit. Discovered during release v1.0.9 remediation (discovered-from:WL-0MSG80FQ9000C8GE).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The canonical full-suite command set for ContextHub (as resolved by full_suite_commands()) matches the suites that actually exist in the repo.
- [ ] run_tests.py --summary --suite all reports green for every suite in the canonical set at a green HEAD.
data.title: Audit auto-green-run never works for ContextHub: NODE_SUITE_DIRS includes tests/node which does not exist
